citations.quote: Efficacy of axitinib is based on a single randomized, open-label, multicenter Phase 3 trial comparing axitinib to sorafenib as second-line systemic therapy in patients with metastatic renal cell carcinoma.

design.text: Single randomized, open-label, multicenter trial comparing axitinib to sorafenib as second-line therapy; patients randomized 1:1 to axitinib 5 mg po BID or sorafenib 400 mg po BID. Protocol was granted an SPA.

citations.quote: Efficacy of axitinib is based on a single randomized, open-label, multicenter Phase 3 trial comparing axitinib to sorafenib as second-line systemic therapy in patients with metastatic renal cell carcinoma. Patients were randomized to receive either axitinib 5 mg po BID or sorafenib 400 mg po BID. The primary efficacy endpoint was PFS as assessed by a blinded Independent Review Committee. Secondary endpoints included overall survival and objective response rate (ORR), and safety of axitinib. This protocol was granted an SPA.
Patients were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to axitinib at a starting dose of 5 mg BID administered orally with food, or sorafenib at a starting dose of 400 mg BID administered orally without food.

population.text: Patients with advanced/metastatic RCC with a clear cell component who had progressed after one prior systemic first-line regimen for mRCC; ECOG performance status 0 or 1.

citations.quote: Key eligibility criteria included histologically- or cytologically-confirmed diagnosis of RCC with a component of clear cell subtype, and with evidence of metastatic disease; one prior systemic first-line regimen for metastatic RCC; no evidence of uncontrolled hypertension; adequate organ function; an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 or 1; and a life expectancy of

endpoint.text: Progression-free survival (PFS) as assessed by a blinded Independent Review Committee

citations.quote: The primary efficacy endpoint was PFS as assessed by a blinded Independent Review Committee.
A total of 723 patients were randomized to receive axitinib or sorafenib.
Overall ITT	N=361	N=362

result.text: Statistically significant improvement in PFS: median PFS 6.7 months (axitinib) vs 4.7 months (sorafenib); HR=0.67 (95% CI 0.54, 0.81); p<0.0001. ORR 19.4% vs 9.4%. No difference in overall survival (OS HR 0.97, 95% CI 0.80, 1.17).

citations.quote: A statistically significant improvement in PFS was demonstrated in patients receiving axitinib compared to patients receiving sorafenib (HR=0.67; 95% CI: 0.54, 0.81; p<0.0001, log-rank test). The median PFS of patients receiving axitinib was 6.7 months (95% CI: 6.3, 8.6) compared to a median PFS of 4.7 months (95% CI: 4.6, 5.6) for patients on the sorafenib arm. This improvement in PFS was greater in the cytokine-treated subgroup compared to the sunitinib-refractory subgroup. There was no difference in the final overall survival analysis between the two arms with a hazard ratio of 0.97 (95% CI 0.8-1.17). Please see table below.

indication.text: INLYTA is indicated for the treatment of advanced renal cell carcinoma (RCC) after failure of one prior systemic therapy.

citations.quote: “INLYTA is indicated for the treatment of advanced renal cell carcinoma (RCC) after failure of one prior systemic therapy.”
This new drug application provides for the use of Inlyta® (axitinib) for the treatment of advanced renal cell carcinoma after failure of one prior systemic therapy.

target_moa.text: Axitinib is a kinase inhibitor that inhibits receptor tyrosine kinases including vascular endothelial growth factor receptors (VEGFR)-1, VEGFR-2, and VEGFR-3, which are implicated in pathologic angiogenesis, tumor growth, and cancer progression.

citations.quote: Axitinib has been shown to inhibit receptor tyrosine kinases including vascular endothelial growth factor receptors (VEGFR)-1, VEGFR-2, and VEGFR-3 at therapeutic plasma concentrations. vote.text: ODAC convened; in response to whether the benefit:risk evaluation was favorable for axitinib in advanced RCC after first-line failure, all 13 members voted "yes" (unanimous, no abstentions).

citations.quote: Because axitinib is an NME, this NDA was presented to Oncology drug Advisory Committee (ODAC). In response to the question “Is the benefit:risk evaluation favorable for axitinib treatment in patients with advanced RCC after failure of a first-line systemic therapy?” All 13 members responded with a unanimous “yes” and there were no abstentions.
